A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Shuffle-R1 study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-G are available and readable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training experiments, benchmark evaluations, ablations, and efficiency analyses in Section 5, with additional comparisons and qualitative results in Appendices F-G.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including the benchmark and ablation tables, training curves, experience-replay comparison, and qualitative case studies.

M1.justification: Sections 4.2-4.3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same Pairwise Trajectory Sampling and Advantage-based Batch Shuffle procedures. The objectives, reward combination, model components, and prompt design are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use Geometry3K, the K12 subset, and the MM-Eureka/Geometry3K mixture for training. In-domain evaluation and coverage of MathVerse, MathVision, MathVista, WeMath, HallusionBench, and ChartQA remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: GRPO and DAPO in Tables 1-2, the model roster in Table 3, RLOO and REINFORCE++ in Appendix Table 8, and prioritized experience replay in Figure 11.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendices C-E retain the same sample counts, model sizes, batch sizes, 80/150-step training budgets, preprocessing, and evaluation procedures. Removing the GPU model designation reduces documentation specificity without establishing a changed experimental setting.

E4.justification: The component and design ablations in Tables 4-5, hyperparameter sweeps in Figure 6, training-efficiency analyses, experience-replay comparison in Appendix F, and case studies in Appendix G are retained without changes.

E5.justification: Both versions report average pass@1 over eight independent evaluation runs in Appendix E. Run-count disclosure and statistical reporting practices are unchanged; no seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Reported scores, plotted results, rankings, and qualitative outputs match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Shuffle-R1's 3B Geometry3K accuracy remains 47.88 in Table 1, and its 7B average remains 64.7 in Table 3.

T1.justification: Equations 1-13 retain the same objective, advantage calculation, sampling definitions, and reward formulas. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same identified inefficiencies, two-component contribution, and claims about training efficiency and generalization. Their scientific scope and strength are unchanged.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the explanations of advantage collapsing and rollout silencing, over-pruning and shuffle saturation, possible overfitting to historical replay samples, and case-study outcomes. No substantive limitations or qualifications are added.

D1.justification: v3 removes H800 from the hardware description in Section 5.1 and NVIDIA H800 from Appendix C, retaining GPU count and memory capacity. It also replaces the first-page direct code-repository link with a project-page link. Other implementation details are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish changed hardware or resource availability.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to existing RL methods remain unchanged. The project-link replacement does not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 removes the first three authors' asterisks, adjusts the internship footnote, and changes the resource label from Code to Project Page. Section ordering, terminology, and the scientific narrative otherwise remain stable.

P2.justification: There is limited local reflow of the author block, first-page footnote, and shortened hardware passage. All 15 figures and eight tables retain their displays, captions, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: The scientific content and supporting evidence remain unchanged, but removing the specific GPU identity from Section 5.1 and Appendix C makes the computing setup less reproducible, particularly for an efficiency-focused paper. The administrative edits and project-link replacement provide no demonstrated offsetting quality gain within the PDFs.
